name: Scanned PDF Tables → Excel
tagline: Scanned or text, its tables come out as Excel — read by OCR on your own GPU, nothing uploaded.
description:
Scanned PDF Tables → Excel turns a PDF's tables into a real .xlsx — one sheet per page — entirely on your own device. Nothing is ever uploaded, and this app has no network access at all.

IT READS PHOTOCOPIES. A scanned page is just a picture: there is no text in it to extract. This app renders the page and actually reads it, with the same three-stage OCR the industry uses — text detection, text recognition, and table-structure analysis that recovers the row and column grid rather than a wall of words. It runs on your GPU through WebGPU, and falls back to the processor where there is no GPU. It tells you which one ran.

IT STILL READS TEXT PDFs EXACTLY. Page by page, it checks whether there is a real text layer. If there is, it reads the numbers instead of guessing at them — no OCR involved. That matters for SERFF insurance rate and rule filings, which is what this was built for: they arrive as born-digital rate tables with scanned exhibits bound in, and you want each page handled the right way. Sheets are labelled, so an OCR reading is never mistaken for an exact one later.

HONEST ABOUT LIMITS. OCR is a reading, not a transcript: a faint, skewed or handwritten page will come back imperfect, and you should check the numbers that matter. Where the structure model cannot see a table, the app lays the text out by position instead and says so.

Everything — all three models and the inference engine — is packed inside the GIF. There is no download after install and no server anywhere. The filing you drop in, and the spreadsheet that comes out, never leave this device.

Its smaller sibling, PDF Tables → Excel, stays the tiny text-only option if you never touch scans.
author: GifOS
